correctness.rationale: The endpoint proof combines a nonincreasing coercive quadratic energy with the polarization identity e^T G(w)=-w^T A w; on every nonzero critical eigenspace state this forces nonzero mean drift, leaving only the equilibrium in the LaSalle invariant zero set. Circulant normality supplies the converse instability outside the spectral window.

originality.rationale: Kerin--Engler prove the strict open stability window and locate the spectral thresholds, but the checked version does not close the semidefinite endpoint. General lossless-quadratic literature explicitly treats negative semidefiniteness as requiring extra information. Targeted searches found no equivalent closed iff theorem or transversality identity in this Lorenz-96 setting; residual publisher-text coverage risk is stated.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly identifies the nonlinear global-stability window with the closed linear spectral window for a broad Lorenz-96-type class and covers Hopf, double-Hopf, and pitchfork critical endpoints in one argument.
